job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
• Broad remit reporting to the CFO
  • Parramatta area | ASAP start temp role with a view to permanent | Circa $120k + Super, depending on experience
  • International business with global engineering and manufacturing capability

Our client, an established international business with Australian operations, is seeking a hands-on Financial Accountant with strong financial reporting and control experience.
Working closely with the CFO, you will deliver timely reporting, maintain the integrity of the accounts, and support the business’s compliance obligations. The role also provides exposure to cash flow, payroll governance and oversight of the payables and receivables functions.

The Role
  • Take ownership of month-end accounting, including journals, accruals, prepayments, intercompany transactions and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Month end reporting including quarterly and annual group reporting.
  • Maintain general ledger accuracy, investigate variances and resolve reconciling items.
  • Prepare ATO and compliance requirements, including BAS, FBT, payroll tax and income tax supporting schedules.
  • Oversee the payroll function and payroll-related accounting and compliance across PAYG, superannuation, payroll tax and STP.
  • Provide day-to-day guidance to finance support staff and oversee the accuracy and timeliness of accounts payable and receivable activities.
  • Monitor cash flow and working capital, providing visibility over outstanding balances and inventory-related financial impacts.
  • Improve reporting processes, accounting procedures and internal controls.

What you’ll bring:
  • CA or CPA qualifications with minimum 5 years financial accounting experience
  • Strong technical accounting skills and experience delivering month-end close and financial reporting.
  • A sound understanding of Australian statutory reporting and tax obligations.
  • Confidence working with payroll providers and reviewing payroll-related accounting and compliance.
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and a practical approach to resolving issues.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both finance and operational colleagues.
  • Experience within an international or group-reporting environment would be advantageous.

How to apply:
Please apply by submitting your resume (in Word format) via the "Apply Now" tab to be considered for the role.

 What next:
Applications will be reviewed for this role and only suitable applicants will be contacted.

job.title: Accounts Receivable Specialist
job.description:
Accounts Receivable Specialist
  • Matraville location - 3 days WFH | 6-month temporary assignment
  • Take ownership of a standalone Accounts Receivable function
  • Support a SAP migration through testing, go-live and post-implementation
The opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Accounts Receivable Specialist to join a great team and support them through a significant system transformation.
This is a hands-on opportunity for someone who can confidently manage the full receivable’s function while contributing to a SAP system migration.
The assignment is expected to run for approximately six months, covering the lead-up to January go-live and the subsequent stabilisation period. There may be an opportunity to transition to a permanent position, subject to future business requirements.
In return you will gain some great exposure and make a direct impact to a supporting a significant transformation project for a reputable global brand.

The Role
  • Own end-to-end Accounts Receivable, collections and credit management activities.
  • Proactively manage aged debt, overdue accounts and structured collection and dunning processes.
  • Engage customers by phone and email, negotiate payment outcomes and resolve disputes.
  • Investigate billing discrepancies and work with internal teams to resolve customer queries.
  • Prepare aged debtor reports, collection forecasts and performance reporting.
  • Support month-end and year-end processes, including reconciliations.
  • Partner with Commercial, Customer Service, Operations and Finance to improve collections and working capital performance.
  • Participate in User Acceptance Testing (UAT), record issues and support resolution and retesting.
  • Assist with data migration, cleansing, validation and reconciliation.
  • Support process documentation, business readiness and training activities.
  • Use advanced Excel to analyse receivables data, investigate variances and provide actionable insights.
  • Develop and improve reports that give the business visibility of debtor performance and collection outcomes.
What you’ll bring
  • At least five years’ relevant experience in Accounts Receivable
  • Proven ownership of an end-to-end receivables function
  • Experience supporting a system migration, ERP implementation or major process change, including UAT ideal
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills
  • SAP experience is strongly preferred
  • Strong reconciliation, data analysis and problem-solving skills.
  • Available for an ASAP start and happy to commit to a contract role
  • A degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or a related discipline
  • Power BI, VBA and macro development skills would be an advantage, but are not essential.
How to apply:
Please apply by submitting your resume (in Word format) via the "Apply Now" tab to be considered for the role.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
• Lead service operations and develop a skilled technical team
  • Shape service performance and support an expanding heavy equipment business
  • Western Sydney location | Hands-on leadership with commercial impact
About the Opportunity

Take the lead in a growing heavy equipment business where your technical expertise, leadership and ideas can make a real impact.
An established manufacturer and supplier of premium heavy capital equipment is seeking an experienced Service Manager to lead its service function in Western Sydney.
This is an opportunity to build on an established operation, develop a capable team and shape how the service business grows. You will combine people leadership, technical support and commercial management, with scope to improve processes, strengthen customer relationships and drive profitable service delivery.

Your Role:
  • Manage service and warranty issues through to effective and commercially sound resolution.
  • Develop and implement process controls to improve efficiency, reduce waste and increase profitability.
  • Oversee day-to-day branch operations across service, spare parts, warranty and administration.
  • Manage branch resources and budgets to support efficient, effective and safe service delivery.
  • Lead and support a team of technicians, including performance management, technical support, training and development.
  • Review and follow up service proposals, quotations, deliveries and related customer requirements.
  • Maintain service reporting, analyse activity and performance, and forecast service requirements.
  • Participate in or observe repairs, commissioning and equipment operation as required to support appropriate job planning.
  • Represent the service business with customers, suppliers and government departments.
  • Provide technical and managerial support to the National Manager, sales teams and other branches as required.
About You:

You are a technically capable leader who enjoys developing people, solving problems and improving how a service operation performs.

You will bring:
  • Experience managing a service, technical support, aftermarket or product support function within heavy equipment, capital equipment, industrial machinery or a similar environment.
  • Strong technical knowledge across mechanical, hydraulic and/or electrical systems.
  • A track record of leading, coaching and developing technical teams.
  • Commercial and operational capability across budgets, resource planning, reporting and forecasting.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to work effectively with customers, colleagues and technical and commercial stakeholders.
  • A hands-on approach, with the willingness to provide technical support and participate in workshop and service activities when required.
  • A degree or higher qualification in mechanical, hydraulic or electrical engineering will be highly regarded; equivalent trade experience and technical skills will also be considered.
Why Join?
  • Join an established, globally backed business entering an exciting period of growth.
  • Take ownership of a service function with scope to shape its development.
  • Lead a capable technical team and support their continued growth.
  • Work with a premium heavy equipment portfolio.
  • Turn your ideas into practical improvements that strengthen service delivery and profitability.
  • Enjoy a varied leadership role combining technical involvement, customer relationships and commercial responsibility.
  • Western Sydney location.
Apply Now! Bring your technical expertise and leadership experience to a business where you can help shape the next stage of growth. 

How to Apply
Please apply by submitting your resume (in Word format) via the "Apply Now" tab to be considered for the role.

job.title: Boutique Manager
job.description:
Do you love fashion, and the chance to make a difference? Alexander Appointments is proud to partner with Pink Finss Charity to find a Boutique Manager for Reloved, its curated pre-loved fashion boutique in Sydney’s Hawkesbury District.

Boutique Manager
  • Windsor location | Approx. 30 hours per week | Rostered shifts Monday to Saturday
  • Lead a curated pre-loved fashion boutique with a meaningful local purpose
  • Help support Hawkesbury people and families affected by cancer

Alexander Appointments is proud to partner with Pink Finss Charity to recruit a Boutique Manager for Reloved, its growing pre-loved fashion boutique in the Hawkesbury. Reloved offers quality pre-loved fashion, accessories and premium brands in a welcoming boutique setting. Every sale helps Pink Finss support local people and families affected by cancer. If you love fashion, enjoy leading people and know how to create a store customers want to return to, this is an opportunity to put your retail experience to work for a cause that matters.

The Role
You’ll lead Reloved’s day-to-day operations, creating an exceptional experience for customers while keeping the boutique beautifully presented and commercially focused. Working closely with volunteers and the Warehouse team, you will:
 
  • Lead, train and support volunteers, building an engaged and welcoming team.
  • Deliver excellent customer service and strengthen relationships with the local community.
  • Select, price and merchandise quality pre-loved fashion and accessories, regularly refreshing stock and displays.
  • Monitor sales, identify opportunities to improve performance and support in-store promotions and events.
  • Maintain accurate pricing, tagging and stock processes, and coordinate stock flow with the Warehouse team.
  • Share featured pieces, styling ideas and boutique stories with Pink Finss’ social media provider.
  • Maintain high standards of store presentation, organisation and safety.


About You
You’re a hands-on retail professional with an eye for fashion and the confidence to take ownership of a boutique. You’ll bring:
  • Experience in retail management, boutique fashion or a similar customer-focused role.
  • Strong people skills and the ability to guide and motivate volunteers.
  • A flair for styling and visual merchandising, backed by sound commercial judgement.
  • Excellent customer service, organisation and attention to detail.
  • The initiative to work independently and the ability to collaborate across the charity.
  • A genuine commitment to Pink Finss’ purpose and the Hawkesbury community.

Experience working with volunteers or in a not-for-profit setting is highly regarded, but the right attitude, energy and passion are just as important.

What’s on Offer?
 
  • A part-time role of approximately 30 hours per week, with shifts rostered Monday to Saturday.
  • The chance to shape the next stage of growth for a distinctive, purpose-led boutique.
  • A supportive team of staff and volunteers, with the freedom to bring your ideas and eye for style to the role.
  • The satisfaction of knowing your work helps local people and families affected by cancer.

How to Apply
Please apply by submitting your resume in Word format via the “Apply Now” tab to be considered for this opportunity. Please include a brief cover letter outlining your relevant retail leadership experience and why you would like to join Reloved and Pink Finss Charity.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Alexander Appointments. Only suitable applicants will be contacted.

https://www.alexanderappointments.com.au/job-results

We are currently seeking an experienced Credit Manager to lead a complex, high-volume credit and accounts receivable function within a global logistics organisation.

Reporting to the National Credit Manager, this is a hands-on leadership role responsible for a large team and multiple key functions across master data, collections and payment allocations. You will provide leadership and direction across the broader team while remaining closely involved in customer escalations, complex accounts and day-to-day operational performance.

This is an opportunity for an experienced Credit Manager who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, leading through complexity and finding practical solutions to improve both customer outcomes and financial performance.

  • Lead and develop a large Credit & Accounts Receivable team across key functional areas
  • Oversee master data, collections and payment allocation functions to ensure effective and accurate delivery
  • Manage complex customer accounts, escalations and collection matters, working closely with internal stakeholders and customers
  • Monitor aged debt, account performance, cash collections and key operational metrics
  • Provide coaching, support and development to Supervisors and their teams
  • Ensure credit and AR processes, controls and policies are consistently applied
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, systems and team performance
  • Work closely with finance, operations, customer and other internal teams to resolve issues and support effective outcomes
  • Provide hands-on leadership in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment
  • Support the National Credit Manager with reporting, analysis and broader credit initiatives

About you

We are looking for an experienced Credit Manager / Senior Credit professional who is comfortable leading a sizeable and complex AR function. You will be someone who can operate at both a strategic and hands-on level - providing direction to your leadership team while also being prepared to get involved in complex customer issues when required.

You will ideally bring:

  • Previous experience managing a large Credit / Accounts Receivable function
  • Strong people leadership experience, including managing through Supervisors or team leaders
  • Experience working across collections, payment allocations, master data or similar AR functions
  • Strong knowledge of credit management and collections processes within a high-volume environment
  • Confidence managing complex customer accounts and escalations
  • Strong negotiation, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills
  • A commercially minded and analytical approach, with the ability to interpret data and make sound decisions
  • Experience driving process improvement and operational efficiencies
